transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… I suppose it’s mostly school. I teach secondary, and normally I’m quite good at separating work things from personal things, you know, staff emails, notices, the morning announcements over the speaker… but lately I can’t shake this feeling that some of them are really about me. Like they’re written in a sort of coded way.

I know that sounds odd. My colleagues have shown me, very kindly, that the same emails went to everyone, and of course announcements are for the whole school. But still, I keep feeling there’s another meaning in them, aimed at me. It’s been hard to let go of, and I thought… well, maybe I should talk to someone before it gets any more distracting.
How long have you been experiencing this feeling that emails and announcements are secretly about you?

About four months, I think. It’s hard to put an exact date on it because school terms all blur together, don’t they—there was that stretch with reports and parents’ evening, and I remember thinking the notices had a funny sort of… angle to them then.

So yes, the worries about the coded messages have been going on maybe four months. And around the same time there’s been that voice I sometimes answer, though I don’t always like saying that out loud.
Over these past four months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or low, or on the other end, unusually elated, energetic, or needing little sleep?

I’m not sure, really. I mean, teaching can make anyone feel worn down, especially by the end of term—there’s always some new policy or someone’s lost exercise book turning up in the wrong cupboard, that sort of thing.

I wouldn’t say I’ve been… dramatically low or anything. And not elated either, not like I’m suddenly full of energy. Sleep varies a bit, but then it always does when there’s marking, doesn’t it? I suppose I haven’t noticed a big mood change, if that’s what you mean.
Have you had any recent medical illnesses, started any new medications, or used alcohol or recreational drugs around the time these experiences began?

I don’t think so… not that I can pin down, anyway. I mean, I had the usual colds that go round school—there’s always something when you’ve got hundreds of pupils coughing into the same corridors—but nothing I’d call a proper illness.

Medications… I’m trying to think. No, I don’t think I started anything new. I’m quite boring with that sort of thing, really. And drink—maybe the odd glass of wine, you know, but not… not around this in any particular way. Recreational drugs, no. I wouldn’t even know where to begin with that, honestly.
Can you describe this voice a bit more—does it talk directly to you, comment on what you're doing, or perhaps discuss you with another voice?

It’s usually just one voice, I think—a woman’s voice. Not someone I can place, which is odd because I’m quite good with voices at school, you know, you learn to tell which child is whispering without even turning round.

It tends to happen when the house is quiet, or after the classroom’s emptied out and everything has that echo-y feeling. She’ll say my name, or make a little comment about what I’m doing—nothing long, just a short sort of remark. It’s clear enough that I sometimes answer, and then I realize there’s no one there.

Have these experiences affected your ability to teach, manage your classroom, or interact with colleagues and friends—have you noticed any decline in how well you're able to function at work or socially?

I’m still teaching, yes. I mean, I get through the day, take the register, explain the lesson, all that. It’s not as if I’ve stopped going in.

But… there have been a few lessons, especially the project ones, where I’ve had to ask one of the others to step in for bits of it. Group work can get very messy, can’t it? Glue sticks everywhere, someone’s poster half-finished, three pupils asking different questions at once—actually, I used to quite like that sort of controlled chaos.

And planning meetings… I’ve needed help getting through those sometimes. A colleague will sort of nudge things along or cover something I should have prepared. I don’t like admitting that.

Outside school, I suppose I’ve become less reliable. Book club, theatre trips, little neighborhood things—I keep saying I’ll go and then I don’t, or I forget, or I just can’t quite manage it. People have noticed, I think.

Have you noticed any changes in your emotions or motivation lately—for example, feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, having a harder time expressing feelings, or just feeling emotionally flat or numb?

Yes… I think so. Not that I don’t care, because I do. I still care about my students, and my friends. If one of the children is upset, I still notice, you know? I’m not made of stone.

But for months now it’s felt like the warmth has sort of… leaked out of things. That sounds dramatic. I used to be the one organizing theatre tickets—there’s this little place that does surprisingly good productions, though the seats are murder on your back—and now I just let it all slide. Book club too. I’ll see the message and think, yes, I should reply, and then somehow I don’t.

Even simple phone calls feel like a hill to climb unless someone really pushes me. It’s not that I want to be rude. I just don’t seem to have the drive I used to.

Have others mentioned that your speech seems disorganized, hard to follow, or that you've been behaving in unusual or disorganized ways—like trouble organizing daily tasks or appearing confused in your actions?

Yes… a bit. I wouldn’t say I’m wandering around doing anything terribly dramatic, but people have noticed I get… stuck.

In lessons, or in the art-fair meetings, I’ll suddenly stop what I’m meant to be doing and start lining up the markers, or straightening papers into some very particular order. It’s silly, really—like the blue ones can’t be next to the orange ones, or the handouts need to be just so. And then the children are waiting, or someone’s asked me a question, and I’ve lost the thread.

Sometimes someone will say something and instead of answering properly I’ll sort of repeat their phrase back. Not meaning to be rude. It just comes out, and then I realize I haven’t actually responded. That’s when I feel embarrassed, because it interrupts things and people look at me a bit oddly.

latest_inference.note: The addition of disorganized behavior (stereotyped ordering rituals, echolalia-like repetition), clear negative symptoms (avolition, affective flattening), and persistent auditory hallucinations alongside referential delusions fulfills broader schizophrenia criteria (>1 month, functional decline) and goes beyond the narrower definition of persistent delusional disorder (F22), which excludes prominent hallucinations, disorganization, and negative symptoms. F22 is therefore ruled out.
